title: Nutrition and Swelling
official: Impact of Perioperative Nutritional Supplementation on Limb Circumference Following Elective Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Prospective Study
summary: This study tests whether taking an essential amino acid (EAA) dietary supplement, Xcelerated Recovery (XR), around the time of knee replacement surgery changes the normal swelling that happens during recovery. Adults 40 years of age or older with knee osteoarthritis who are having a robotic-assisted total knee replacement at UCSF, and who screen positive for nutritional risk or reduced muscle strength, will be randomly assigned to standard care plus XR or to standard care alone. Swelling will be measured with a tape measure by a team member who does not know which group the participant is in. All participants will also use a temporary skin sensor and smartphone app (InkWell) that measures knee swelling, range of motion, and skin temperature.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults 40 years of age or older with knee osteoarthritis
* Nutritional risk based on a score less than or equal to 11 on the Mini Nutritional Assessment-Short Form (MNA-SF) and/or reduced muscle strength and function based on a score greater than or equal to 4 on the SARC-F
* Elective primary unilateral robotic-assisted TKA for osteoarthritis
* Body mass index (BMI) between 18.5 and 30 kg/m²
* Able to provide written informed consent
* Willing to comply with supplementation and follow-up
* Owns a smartphone compatible with the InkWell Health app (iPhone with iOS 13 or later, or Android 5 or later), or has a caregiver with a compatible smartphone who can assist with scans

Exclusion Criteria:

* Revision arthroplasty
* Arthroplasty for inflammatory arthropathy, rheumatoid arthritis, or trauma
* Active cancer or severe metabolic disorder
* Chronic lower-extremity edema
* Preoperative ankle swelling
* Lymphedema
* Peripheral vascular disease
* History of deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
* Severe renal insufficiency
* Illicit drug use
* Known allergy to supplement ingredients
* Inability to consent
